format: Sequences of acts on one namespace registry (patterns/namespace), each step with the verdict the pattern gives it: 'accepted', or the refusal code. Every sequence starts at an empty registry whose log id is `registry`. A step's `at` is the registry's clock, an instant as protocol/conventions writes it. A `statement` is a claim, grant, transfer or catalog release the registry decides by Deciding a statement and, if accepted, appends; a release's `index` is the text of the index it names, carried with it. A `verify` is a catalog release offered to a verifier, which decides it by Verifying a release against this registry's log as it stands at that step: a release verifies only when the log holds its exact bytes. A `ruling` is the hub owner's, recorded in the log. A `revoke` is the hub revoking that key's identity (patterns/principal-identity); the registry records nothing, the step's verdict is always accepted, and the identity is not enrolled for every later step. Each signature's `by` names the key it says it was made with; in one step it was made with another, and is refused. `state` is every listed namespace's state after the last step: status, holder and grants by key name, an absent grants meaning none. `enrolled` is every identity the registry's hub has enrolled, by key name, with its kind and the identity the key belongs to: two keys of one identity are one person's keys before and after an identity rotation (protocol/identity, Key Rotation); any other key is not enrolled. `never_claimable` holds a sample of the place and issuer codes a registry refuses, each one the corpus states (a standard's applies_in, the start of a standard's id); a registry refuses every such code (schemas/names), not only these.
keys: Every key is named as in vectors/fixed-form-statements.json, which holds its seed, public key and fingerprint; a key's fingerprint is what a field holds.
made_with: github.com/cloudflare/circl v1.6.5, FIPS 204 deterministic signing, as vectors/fixed-form-statements.json

sequences.case: the first claim takes the name; a second claim of it, by anyone, is refused, and the first claim's own bytes sent again are a replay
reserved names, place and issuer codes, names confusable with a reserved name, and names outside the grammar are refused, and none is held after

a service identity, an identity the hub never enrolled, a claim signed by someone other than its holder, a signature made by another key than the one it names, another registry's claim, a stale claim and a malformed time are each refused, and the name stays unheld
a transfer signed by one side is refused; signed by both it moves the namespace and ends the outgoing holder's grants; the outgoing holder then holds nothing, and a service identity cannot take it on

a rotation signed by both keys of one identity moves the namespace to the incoming key and keeps its grants; the outgoing key can no longer act, a grantee from before the rotation still publishes, and a 'rotation' to another person's key, signed by both, is refused, since a hand-over to another identity is a transfer
a retirement names no incoming holder; once retired, the name is never claimed again, by its last holder or anyone, and nothing is granted, released or reassigned under it

ruling.reason: a ruling never un-retires a namespace

sequences.case: a frozen namespace accepts no grant and is still held; a reassignment moves it and ends its grants, and the earlier holder can no longer act; a reassignment only to an enrolled user, and no ruling on a name nobody claimed; a reassignment of a frozen namespace changes its holder and leaves it frozen

ruling.reason: a dispute over who holds the name
the holder's key was lost; the name goes to the person the decision names
a reassignment to an identity this hub never enrolled
a reassignment to a service identity
a freeze of a name nobody claimed
a second dispute over who holds the name
the dispute is decided for the earlier holder, and the name stays frozen until a ruling unfreezes it

sequences.case: a release is an act at the registry, accepted only while its signer is the holder or a publish grantee whose identity the hub has enrolled and not revoked: withdrawing the grant ends it, a revoked grantee cannot release, a release naming another registry is refused here, a namespace nobody claimed has no releases, and a release the log recorded still verifies after its signer's grant and identity have ended; the same bytes signed by a key the log did not record them under are not that release

a release counts once the registry's log records it, and is judged at the registry's clock, never at a time its signer wrote: the holder's old key, rotated out, cannot release afterwards, even dated back inside its own time, and a verifier refuses that release as unrecorded however it was offered; a release the old key made before the rotation still verifies; the incoming key's next release is not pre-empted; after a transfer neither the outgoing holder nor its grantees release; a number already recorded cannot be given a second index; and a release dated beyond the replay window is refused

a release continues the latest one the log records: its number is the next, its previous is that release's index, and its index keeps every ref, a retired one still retired; an index whose text is not the digest the release signed is malformed, and a recorded release sent again is a replay

a holder whose identity the hub has revoked can no longer grant, transfer, rotate or retire the namespace, each refused as NAMESPACE_IDENTITY_UNKNOWN and nothing recorded; a ruling hands it on, and the new holder acts
